rounds.text: Bajaj Auto Ltd is significantly undervalued by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 22x [E1] while delivering an extraordinary rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E64]. The company's fundamental performance is exceptional, highlighted by a staggering 48% compounded sales growth and 57% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21], vastly outperforming historical rates [E14, E18]. This commercial momentum is backed by elite profitability metrics, including a 29.2% ROE [E13] and a 28.2% ROCE [E12], alongside robust free cash flow generation of nearly INR 5,200 crores in the first 9 months of the year, representing a 70% increase over the prior year [E89]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation via discounted cash flow points to a fair value of Rs 17,647 per share, leaving a substantial margin of safety of 40.6% [E45, E46]. Market leadership is firmly entrenched through an overwhelming 70% plus share in the ICE motorcycle segment and an 85% plus share in the CNG segment [E87], while international expansion is scaling rapidly with exports crossing 600,000 units after 15 quarters [E80]. Conceded: the stock trades at a high price-to-book ratio of 7.87x and exhibits a low cash conversion of 0.25x for Mar 2026 [E2, E34]. Nevertheless, with capital expenditure largely completed as evidenced by an 86.8% drop in CWIP [E40] and management actively aiming for its highest-ever top-line performance in USD terms [E76], the current valuation fails to capture this fundamental strength.

Bajaj Auto trades at a lofty price-to-book multiple of 7.87x against a book value of ₹1,332 [E2], and its EV/EBITDA of 16.77x stands at a steep premium compared to the sector benchmark of 11.37x [E11]. Beneath headline earnings growth, the cash conversion ratio sits at a worrying 0.25x for Mar 2026 because reported profits far outpace actual operating cash flow [E34]. Furthermore, borrowings have expanded to ₹26,401 Cr in Sep 2026 from ₹22,713 Cr a year prior [E39], while foreign institutional ownership has dropped by 5.77 percentage points since Dec 2023 [E42] alongside a negative institutional money flow signal [E44]. Operational headwinds are also evident as raw material pressures mount, highlighted by management acknowledging that noble metals and base metals like aluminium and copper continue to harden [E91], alongside a ₹61 crore exceptional charge for new labour code wage definitions [E92]. Conceded: the company boasts a high return on equity [E60], healthy dividend payouts [E61], and strong recent sales growth [E65].

Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is 7.87x [E2] and the EV/EBITDA multiple of 16.77x trades above the sector benchmark of 11.37x [E11]. However, that premium valuation is entirely justified by elite capital efficiency, evidenced by an extraordinary ROA of 14.16% against a sector benchmark of 6.54% [E8] and an ROCE of 24.52% compared to the sector's 12.77% [E10]. While the bear flags cash conversion at 0.25x for March 2026 [E34], that snapshot ignores that operating cash flow reached ₹2,597 Cr and free cash flow hit ₹1,885 Cr for the same period [E35, E36], alongside nearly ₹5,200 crores in free cash flow generated in the first nine months—up 70% year-on-year [E89]. Conceded: borrowings rose to ₹26,401 Cr in September 2026 [E39], but this is backed by massive liquidity including about ₹15,000 crores in surplus cash [E88] and a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.72x [E37]. Furthermore, capital expenditure cycle pressures are resolving as capital work-in-progress (CWIP) dropped by 86.8% [E40], signaling that new capacity is coming online [E40] just as management targets its highest ever top-line performance in USD terms [E76]. Finally, foreign institutional holding shifts [E42] are offset by domestic institutions raising their stake by 4.53 percentage points [E43] and promoters increasing ownership [E41].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached ₹2,597 Cr and free cash flow hit ₹1,885 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], alongside nearly ₹5,200 crores in free cash flow generated over the first nine months [E89]. However, this does not excuse the cash conversion ratio collapsing to 0.25x for March 2026, which clearly signals that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash and demands close scrutiny of receivables and accruals [E34]. While the bull points to massive liquidity and a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.72x [E37], borrowings actually expanded to ₹26,401 Cr in September 2026, up from ₹22,713 Cr a year earlier [E39]. Conceded: CWIP dropped by 86.8% [E40], but the valuation still commands a hefty price-to-book of 7.87x [E2] and an EV/EBITDA of 16.77x against a sector benchmark of 11.37x [E11]. Furthermore, the claim that institutional shifts are benign is contradicted by negative institutional money flow and a drop in foreign institutional holding from 14.64% in December 2023 to 8.87% by September 2026 [E42, E44, E69].

evidence.quote: We expect this growth momentum in the industry to continue and the motorcycle industry to continue to grow at, say, 12% to 15%.

evidence.fact: Management expects export growth tempo to continue in the coming months and aims to deliver the highest ever top line performance in USD terms this financial year.
evidence.quote: Overall, the Exports business has established a sustained growth momentum, and we expect this growth tempo to continue in the coming months. In fact, the business is on the path to deliver its highest ever top line performance in USD terms this financial year.

evidence.fact: The company expects to outpace industry growth in the 125cc plus and 150cc plus segments.
evidence.quote: Therefore, we expect to outpace industry growth in the 125cc plus segment and particularly in the 150cc plus segment and continue on the path of market share acquisition, which has commenced a couple of months ago.

evidence.fact: Management noted that the top 30 overseas markets grew by about 10% in the quarter while company sales grew at 15%.
evidence.quote: The top 30 overseas markets collectively accounting for nearly 75% of the emerging market, industry grew by about 10% in this quarter with our sales growing at 15%, thereby signalling an increase of market share in these key markets.

evidence.fact: The motorcycle industry grew by about 15% post GST rationalization in Q3.
evidence.quote: But post the GST rationalization, Q3 has grown by about 15% in the industry.

evidence.fact: Export volumes crossed the 600,000 units mark after 15 quarters.
evidence.quote: The BU crossed the 200,000 average per month sales level in October '25 after nearly 40 months and maintained this level through the remainder of the quarter, surpassing the 600,000 units mark after 15 quarters.

evidence.fact: The company strategically invested slightly above INR2,300 crores during the first 9 months into its Netherlands subsidiary BAIHBV and in the growth of BACL.
evidence.quote: We have strategically invested slightly above INR2,300 crores during this 9-month period into our Netherlands subsidiary, BAIHBV which you would recall was partly to fund the KTM acquisition and in the growth of BACL, which has steadily grown in scale and footprint.

evidence.fact: Sales in Bajaj Brazil came close to the 10,000 mark supported by expanded production capacities.
evidence.quote: Sales in Bajaj Brazil came in close to 10,000 mark, supported by expanded production capacities and the subsidiary is now delivering a healthy bottom line performance too.

evidence.fact: The distribution network for Chetak expanded to nearly 450 exclusive Chetak stores and 4,000 points of sale across 800 cities and towns.
evidence.quote: The scale-up was also supported by distribution network that expanded to nearly 450 exclusive Chetak stores and 4,000 points of sale across 800 cities and towns.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins expanded to 20.8%, up 30 basis points sequentially.
evidence.quote: EBITDA margins expanded to 20.8%, up 30 basis points sequentially.

evidence.fact: The EV business delivers double-digit EBITDA margin while improving unit economics.
evidence.quote: More importantly, the EV business now delivers double-digit EBITDA margin while improving unit economics as the portfolio continues to scale.

evidence.fact: The net price versus cost inflation hit was nearly 50 basis points on the margin.
evidence.quote: As a result, we saw a net price versus cost inflation hit of nearly 50 basis points on the margin.

evidence.fact: The company maintains a 70% plus market share in the ICE segment with an 85% plus share in the CNG segment.
evidence.quote: We continue to maintain a 70% plus market share in the ICE segment with an overwhelming share of 85% plus in the CNG segment, which is the largest segment within ICE.

evidence.fact: The company closed the quarter with surplus cash of about INR15,000 crores.
evidence.quote: We continue to deliver strong and consistent cash generation, closing the quarter with surplus cash of about INR15,000 crores.

evidence.fact: In the first 9 months of the year, the company generated nearly INR5,200 crores of free cash flow, up 70% over the same period last year.
evidence.quote: It's also worth noting that in the first 9 months of this year, we've generated nearly INR5,200 crores of free cash flow, and that was up 70% over the same period last year, reflecting our strong track record of converting profit to cash.

evidence.fact: The last capital infusion into BACL was in October of about INR300 crores as Tier 2 capital.
evidence.quote: The last infusion we did into BACL was in October of about INR300 crores. And that we think is absolutely the last of it that is needed. In fact, that infusion also went in as Tier 2 capital.

evidence.fact: Noble metals including platinum, palladium, and rhodium saw sharp increases, while aluminium, copper, nickel, and lead continued to harden.
evidence.quote: Noble Metals especially platinum, palladium and rhodium all saw sharp increases, whilst aluminium, copper, nickel and lead also continued to harden.

evidence.fact: The company recognized INR61 crores as a onetime exceptional charge towards past service cost arising from new labour code wage definitions.
evidence.quote: As you're all aware, pursuant to the amendment in the definition of wages under the new labour code, we recognized INR61 crores as a onetime exceptional charge towards the past service cost arising from the changes introduced under the new labour code.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): The top management team exercise for KTM AG will be completed by April 1st.
evidence.quote: Second, build the top management team. The top deck is now largely in place, and the exercise will be completed by 1st April.
